items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: which in a lot of circumstances, Lincoln Goines or any of the cats are in the band well that’s a selling point.

ctx.x: I was going to ask about that. I had an experience a couple of different times in New York where you go to like the Iridium, and by myself I think I spent $60, and I saw a band that had two very well known musicians on it but was obviously an unrehearsed, it was like a throw together gig you know. Which of course is typical. But I didn’t leave feeling great. Because I had to leave after the first set too or pay again. And so as an owner, how do you address my unhappiness?

Well number one is I usually put good shows together so I know that my shows that you’re going to get are going to be good shows. Some of the jazz shows you don’t know who the players are going to be when they come in but for the most part you can tell by knowing, which I know most of the cats so I know what they’re like and I know that they’ll come in with a good band and the whole bit. So as much as I can I get those details ahead of time and post them with everything — who the sidemen are in the band so…

conditions perfect. And you’re going to love the club. And it’s going to be the right gig, that you’re going to want to come back and play my room again. So we’ll set you up a gross potential based on what we feel is a reasonable market value for that show in Buffalo. Then we’ll put you on a percentage above that if you sell it out completely to the hilt, well then you’ll break in a percentage and we’ll get close to the number you’re looking for. And then the next time you come back we’ll raise the price. Well by…
